content: 1. Overview of TB Treatment Regimens and Outcomes The document discusses various TB treatment regimens, including the SA New regimen compared to the WHO-recommended long regimen for drug-resistant TB. Key findings include a 10% reduction in treatment success rates with the SA New regimen, a 71% reduction in treatment failure, a 38% increase in mortality, and a 33% increase in patients lost to follow-up. No significant differences were observed in adverse events of grade 3 or higher. 2. Subgroup Analyses Treatment success was consistently lower across all subgroups except for patients without a history of prior TB. The reduction in success was particularly pronounced in patients with prior TB, HIV-negative status, smear-negative disease, those aged 15 or older, and those with pulmonary TB. 3. Sensitivity Analyses Sensitivity analyses revealed significant heterogeneity in treatment outcomes across different countries and regions. The variability in success rates was influenced by factors such as age, smear status, and HIV status. Large sites in the WHO dataset, such as India and Papua New Guinea, demonstrated higher success rates compared to South Africa. 4. Challenges in Data Interpretation The analysis highlighted challenges in distinguishing the effects of treatment regimens from the influence of settings. 5. NEXT Trial Design and Findings The NEXT trial evaluated a 6to 9-month all-oral regimen (including bedaquiline, linezolid, levofloxacin, and other drugs) for multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB). Conducted across five sites in South Africa, the trial used an open-label RCT design. Eligibility criteria included adults with newly diagnosed pulmonary TB and rifampicin resistance confirmed by at least two susceptibility tests. Exclusion criteria included prior MDR-TB treatment, resistance to fluoroquinolones, and significant comorbidities. 6. Trial Outcomes The primary outcome was defined as a favorable treatment result (cure or treatment completion) without events such as death, treatment failure, relapse, or reinfection at 24 months post-treatment initiation. The trial was terminated early due to changes in the comparator regimen, which incorporated bedaquiline into the South African National TB Program. 7. Treatment Success and Failure In the intervention group, 51% achieved treatment success, while 24% experienced failure or recurrence. In the comparator group, 71% achieved success, and 4% experienced failure. Mortality rates were similar between groups (8-9%). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 35% of participants in both groups. 8. Definitions of Treatment Outcomes Favorable Outcome: Treatment completion or cure with at least three consecutive negative cultures taken 30 days apart after the intensive phase. Unfavorable Outcome: Treatment failure, defined as the need for permanent regimen changes due to lack of culture conversion, bacteriological reversion, acquired resistance, or adverse events. Relapse: Positive culture during follow-up with the same strain as the initial infection. Reinfection: Positive culture during follow-up with a different strain. 9. Reclassification of Outcomes In the intervention group, 12 cases were initially classified as treatment failures. Upon reclassification, 10 of these were found to have converted to negative cultures after regimen changes. Similarly, in the comparator group, 26 cases of failure were reclassified, with 17 achieving culture conversion after regimen adjustments. 10. Implications for TB Treatment Guidelines The findings underscore the need for robust RCTs to guide TB treatment decisions. The variability in outcomes across settings highlights the importance of tailoring regimens to local contexts while ensuring adherence to global guidelines.
